items.title: NORWAY JUST TOLD AI DATA CENTERS TO WAIT IN LINE FOR POWER
items.summary:
NORWAY JUST TOLD AI DATA CENTERS TO WAIT IN LINE FOR POWER

We've been tracking AI money through chips and funding rounds, and this week Norway showed us a different meter. Reuters reported on November 9 that Statnett, the state grid operator, has received about 26,000 megawatts of new connection requests this year. That is more than the roughly 25,000 the whole country draws at peak.

Data centers filed three quarters of those requests. The ones already plugged in draw about 800 megawatts, according to figures published with the pause, so most of the requested load exists only on paper for now.

Headlines call both numbers demand, and we think that mix-up is where the money gets mispriced. Only one of them pays a power bill today.

Statnett has paused new data center reservations, and Bloomberg reported it expects to lift the pause by August 1, 2027. Until then, the scarce input in Nordic AI is a place in the queue, and the government's coming licensing scheme decides who gets one. It has already said crypto mining doesn't qualify.

The cost of that queue may not stay inside the industry. TIME reported in June that power prices in northern Norway are expected to double within two to three years, partly on data center demand, and households pay those prices too.

Cheap Nordic power pulled AI money north. For the next nine months or so, what that money buys is a spot in a line the ministry controls.

Headlines say Anthropic just launched an AI office suite. That's a little ahead of what's actually shipping.

Yesterday in San Francisco they added Claude Sheets and Claude Whiteboards, and they moved Claude Data — it used to be called Dashboards — to general availability on paid plans. These sit on top of the Docs, Slides, and Design tools Claude already had, which is why the coverage reads like a full suite. Interactive connectors also got an upgrade: you can open partner apps like Adobe or Atlassian inside Claude, instead of jumping between tabs.

What's usable today is narrower. Sheets and Whiteboards are in beta, and they're on paid plans, not the free tier. Anthropic's product lead has already told reporters that Sheets is still fairly basic. If you need serious spreadsheet work, they pointed people back to the Excel add-in.

Claude Meetings is the piece that sounds like a real workplace shift: add Claude to a call, let it take notes, start the plan, and update the board while people are still talking. Anthropic's own post still says this is coming soon. Some coverage says it's already in beta on Team and Enterprise, starting with Google Meet only. I wouldn't assume it's in your account until you can actually add it to a call.

If you already pay for Claude and spend half your week in messy docs and spreadsheets, this is worth clicking through. Just don't throw out Excel or Google Workspace because of a headline. The new pieces are early, paid, and still sitting next to the tools you already use — not instead of them.

items.title: Half-inverse problems for perturbed Bessel operators with a known left-hand potential
items.summary: For the regular Sturm-Liouville operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+q$ acting in $L^2(0,1)$, the Hochstadt-Lieberman theorem states that one full spectrum together with the potential on either the left half-interval $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ or the right half-interval $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ uniquely determines the full potential $q$. The inverse-square singular term $\tfrac{l(l+1)}{x^2}$ in the perturbed Bessel operator $-\frac{{\rm d}^2}{{\rm d}x^2}+\frac{l(l+1)}{x^2}+q$, acting in $L^2(0,1)$, breaks the left-right symmetry. It is known that, when the right half of the potential $q|_{(1/2,1)}$ is given, the uniqueness of the potential can be established even if a finite number of eigenvalues (depending on $l$) are omitted. In this paper we study the opposite setting--where the left half potential $q|_{(0,1/2)}$ is known--and show that one full spectrum together with finitely many norming constants uniquely determine the full potential $q$. Moreover, we specify the minimum number of norming constants required for the uniqueness. Finally, for positive integer $l$, $L^2$ potentials, and the Dirichlet boundary condition at $x = 1$, we establish the local bi-Lipschitz stability and the local solvability from the full spectrum and finitely many norming constants, assuming the potential on the left half-interval is fixed.

items.title: The Optimal Constant for One-Shot Channel Simulation and Strong Functional Representation Lemma
items.summary: We prove a tight bound for one-shot channel simulation via a stronger version of the strong functional representation lemma: for any random variables $X,Y$, there exists a random variable $Z$ with $I(Z;X)=H(Y|X,Z)=0$ and $H(Y|Z)\le I+\log I+(1-γ)\log e-\log\log e+O(I^{-1}\log I)$, where $I=I(X;Y)$ and $γ$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. A more convenient bound is $H(Y|Z)<I+\log(I+2)+1$. The first bound is notable in the sense that the constant term $(1-γ)\log e-\log\log e$ is optimal, and cannot be improved for any bound stated only in terms of $I$. Hence, this is the tightest form of the strong functional representation lemma up to the third order. We also prove that the Poisson functional representation is almost optimal up to a constant gap, and provide a simple finite-blocklength achievability bound that implies the $(1/2)\log n$ redundancy of the simulation of memoryless non-singular channel. These are proved via a generalization of the functional information, in particular, the exponential functional information, which closely approximates the cost of one-shot channel simulation.

items.title: Early--Narrow and Late--Wide Populations of GRB X-ray Flares
items.summary: The physical origin of gamma-ray burst (GRB) X-ray flares remains debated, particularly whether they arise from prolonged central-engine activity or from variability in the external shock. Building on our previous analysis of 89 Swift GRBs with measured redshifts, we investigate the rest-frame temporal properties of X-ray flares detected in 61 bursts. We apply a multivariate Gaussian Mixture Model to rest-frame peak times and widths. We identify two statistically distinct populations: early-narrow flares (80%), with characteristic peak times of approximately 10^2 s and w/t_pk <= 1, and late-wide flares (20%), with characteristic peak times of ~ 10^3.5 s and w/t_pk >= 2. Of the 61 single or first flares, 55 belong to the early-narrow population and only 6 to the late-wide population. Of the 36 second flares, 23 (64%) belong to the early-narrow population, with shorter waiting times, whereas 13 (36%) belong to the late-wide population, with substantially longer waiting times. The width-peak-time correlation remains significant for early-narrow flares but not for late-wide flares. Furthermore, we find no correlation between flare width and energy. We find a decline of flare luminosity with peak time, driven primarily by the early-narrow population, but not statistically significant for late-wide flares. These results imply that a simple shift in time, potentially associated with later episodes of central-engine activity, cannot explain the distinction between the two flare populations. On the other hand, the peak times are consistent with expectations from an accretion disk formed following the collapse of a stellar-size massive star. Combined with our previous finding that flare properties are independent of the presence of an X-ray plateau, these results favor prolonged accretion-driven central-engine activity over external-shock variability as the primary origin of X-ray flares.

items.title: High-power X-Point Target divertor experiments on the TCV tokamak
items.summary: Stationary power exhaust in the X-Point Target (XPT) divertor configuration is investigated in high-power ($2.5\,\text{MW}$) TCV L-mode discharges, in which the Lengyel detachment scaling metric $P_{\text{SOL}}B_{0}/(R_{0}n_{e,\text{u}}^{2})$ lies in the range expected for reactors (SPARC, ITER, ARC). Compared with a conventional single-null (SN) divertor, the XPT improves power exhaust performance, reducing the peak outer target heat flux by 40--60\% and enabling divertor detachment with nitrogen seeding under conditions in which the SN cannot be detached. Detachment evolves asymmetrically across the multiple XPT outer strike points. The sensitivities of the peak target heat fluxes and impurity emission front positions to the X-point separation ($\text{d}R_{\text{u},X2}$) are characterized and found to decrease at higher nitrogen seeding levels. Field-reversal experiments reveal the critical role of $E\times B$ drifts inherent to the magnetic topology of the secondary X-point, which drive an unconventional redistribution of density and impurity radiation in the XPT divertor and thereby cause the asymmetries between the XPT outer strike points, largely confirming the expectations from recent SOLPS-ITER modelling. A framework for understanding the power exhaust physics of the XPT is presented, detailing the roles of SOL splitting, connection length peaking, $E\times B$ drifts, and vessel geometry. Together, these results establish an experimental physics basis for the XPT divertor as a potential power exhaust solution for tokamak reactors.

items.title: Profinite groups with finite conjugacy classes of commutators
items.summary: It was shown in a recent work by Senise and Shumyatsky that if $G$ is a finite group such that $|x^G|\leq m$ whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, then $G''$ has $m$-bounded order. In this paper, we examine the following question: given a profinite group $G$ such that $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order, does it follow that $G''$ is finite? We show that, in general, the answer to this is negative. The main result obtained in this paper is the following theorem: Let $G$ be a profinite group in which $|x^G|$ is finite whenever $x$ is a commutator of prime power order. Assume that $π(G)$ is finite. Then: (1) The second commutator subgroup $G''$ is finite; (2) $G$ has an open normal subgroup of nilpotency class at most $3$.

items.title: Searching for Planets around Altair with JWST/NIRcam
items.summary: Altair (alpha Aql) is one of the nearest stars to the Sun at 5.13 pc and its age has recently been revised to 88+/-10 Myr, making it one of the youngest stars in the Solar neighborhood. This makes Altair a compelling target for high-contrast direct imaging searches for giant planets. We present two epochs of simultaneous F444W and F200W MASK430R JWST/NIRCam coronagraphic imaging observations. After post-processing, these data achieve F444W contrast levels of 2 x 10^-6 at 1" (5.1 au), 1.5 x 10^-7 at 2" (10.3 au), and a few x 10^-8 beyond 4"(20 au). Using the Sonora Flame Skimmer models, this corresponds to sub-Jupiter mass sensitivity beyond 5 au and sub-Saturn mass sensitivity beyond 10 au. We identified several candidate point sources in the field in the first epoch data. Second epoch observations confirmed that none of the candidates were co-moving with Altair and their colors are consistent with background stars. Altair has no known companions, no detected debris disk, and is not associated with any stellar association. Despite this, its youth and proximity ensure it will remain a high-priority target for future high-contrast imaging observations. We additionally discuss Altair as a potential reference star for future observations, presenting measurements of background sources in the field and showing that Altair will remain at least a few arcsec from background stars over the next 10-20 years, making it a reliable reference target for upcoming imaging campaigns including the Roman Space Telescope Coronagraph Instrument.

items.title: Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
items.summary: In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.

items.title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
items.summary: We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.

items.title: Unpolarized proton PDF with physical quark masses and large momenta
items.summary: We present a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculation of the proton isovector ($u-d$) unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF) at physical sea and valence quark masses, using Coulomb-gauge-fixed quark bilinears within the large-momentum effective theory framework. The calculation is performed on a (2+1)-flavor ensemble with a lattice spacing of $a=0.076$ fm and proton momenta up to $2.3$ GeV. We combine kinematically enhanced nucleon interpolating operators, the Coulomb-gauge method, and high-statistics measurements to improve the signal quality at large momenta and quark separations. We use the static regularization-independent momentum subtraction and hybrid schemes to renormalize the bare matrix elements. The light-cone PDF in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme is obtained from the quasi-PDF through next-to-leading-order (NLO) perturbative matching supplemented by next-to-leading-logarithmic renormalization-group resummation. With reduced uncertainties, the resulting PDF is consistent with our previous calculation on a similar lattice ensemble with $a=0.06$~fm and a valence pion mass of 300 MeV. Notably, despite the reduced uncertainties, the agreement with the phenomenological PDF persists over the longitudinal momentum fraction range $0.25\lesssim|x|\lesssim0.75$, where the lattice calculation is expected to be reliable. This agreement is further supported by a comparison in coordinate space, where our short-distance lattice matrix elements are consistent with those obtained from the phenomenological PDF through NLO matching. In particular, we observe close agreement in the imaginary part for the first time. Together, these results represent an encouraging step toward precision benchmarking of lattice QCD calculations of PDFs.

items.title: Deep Inelastic Scattering and Proton Structure Functions in AdS/QCD models
items.summary: In this work we study the holographical fermionic deep inelastic scattering in a deformed AdS model. Imposing that the potentials that emerge from the Schrödinger-like equations for the fermionic chiral left and right modes are SUSY partners to preserve isospectrality, we implement a systematical truncation of such potentials. Then, we show that in the quadratic approximation of the deformed AdS model, the fermionic DIS and the proton structure functions $F_{1,2}(q^2,x)$ are identical with the results obtained from the soft wall model. Further, we obtain and compare high-order approximations for the fermionic potentials with the full solution of the deformed AdS model and show, as expected, that as greater the order of approximation, the better are the results for $F_{1,2}(q^2,x)$ when compared with experimental data explicitly for the Bjorken parameter values $x=0.85, 0.75$ and $0.65$.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: 2026年11月11日（水）XGBN AIニュース朝刊から要約
items.summary:
2026年11月11日（水）XGBN AIニュース朝刊から要約

【AIが仕事の入り口を奪い合う時代へ】

Anthropicが表計算やホワイトボードをClaudeに組み込み、GoogleはGemini 4 Carbonの提供を開始しました。

OpenAIもChatGPT内に企業の窓口を設ける新機能を発表しました。

AIは回答する道具から、仕事や商取引を行う場所へと変わりつつあります。

【1．ClaudeがOfficeの領域に進出】

Anthropicは『Claude Sheets』『Claude Whiteboards』『Claude Data』を発表しました。

AIとの対話から表計算シートや共同作業用ボードを作成でき、データ分析の結果を共有する機能も拡充しました。

AdobeやAtlassianなどの外部ツールをClaudeの画面内で操作できる仕組みも導入します。

Microsoft OfficeやGoogle Workspaceが担ってきた仕事を、AIの画面内で完結させようとする動きです。

発表直後にMicrosoft株が下落したとの投稿も注目されましたが、短期的な株価変動をこの発表だけの影響と断定することはできません。

=====

【2．Gemini 4 Carbonの提供開始】

Googleは『Gemini 4 Carbon』の提供を開始しました。

複雑な推論、大量の文書の分析、画像を含む情報の理解に重点を置いた高性能モデルです。

Google AI StudioのAPIなどを通じて、有料の開発者や企業が利用できます。

導入期間のAPI価格は100万トークンあたり入力2ドル、出力10ドルで、12月からはそれぞれ4ドル、20ドルになる予定です。

ただし、トークン単価が安くても、同じ仕事を終えるまでの総費用が安いとは限りません。

=====

【3．ChatGPTに企業の公式窓口】

OpenAIは『Businesses in ChatGPT』のベータ版を発表しました。

企業がChatGPT上の自社情報を管理し、利用者の問い合わせに応じる専用AIエージェントを提供できる仕組みです。

利用者は商品やサービスを比較・検討し、そのまま企業との対話へ進めます。

企業が提供する情報に基づく会話は、ChatGPTの通常の回答と区別して表示されます。

検索エンジンや企業サイトが担ってきた顧客接点を、対話型AIが取り込む可能性があります。

一方、広告・企業の説明と中立的な情報を明確に区別することが重要になります。

=====

【4．Gemini Robotics 2.5、器用な作業へ】

Google DeepMindは『Gemini Robotics 2.5』を発表しました。

視覚と言語による理解をロボットの行動につなげるVLAモデルで、より幅広い作業を学習し、習得を速めることを目指しています。

発表では、人型ロボットがリボンを結ぶような、柔らかい物体を扱う作業も紹介されました。

ロボットAIでは、物体を理解するだけでなく、実際の身体を使って正確に操作する能力が課題です。

現時点では提携企業への展開が中心で、あらゆる環境で同じ能力を発揮できるわけではありません。

=====

【5．Mercor、評価額200億ドルに】

AI学習・評価を支援するMercorは、7億5,000万ドルの資金調達を発表しました。

今回の資金調達による企業評価額は200億ドルです。

同社は専門家の知識を活用したAIの学習、評価、企業向けエージェントの開発支援を進めています。

AI競争ではモデルやGPUだけでなく、AIが仕事を正しく遂行できたかを評価する仕組みにも巨額の資金が集まっています。

=====

【全体の総括】

今回のニュースには、3つの大きな流れがあります。

第一に、AIが既存の業務ソフトを取り込み、仕事を始める場所そのものになろうとしています。

第二に、AIが企業と顧客を結ぶ新しい窓口になりつつあります。

第三に、競争の対象がモデルの知能だけでなく、実際の仕事を遂行する能力や、その成果を評価する仕組みに広がっています。

『どのAIが最も賢いか』だけでなく、『誰が仕事の流れ全体を握るか』が、ますます重要になってきました。
